topSignals.title: Twelfth consecutive quiet day for Elcogen and Topsoe, INOCEL's two priority benchmark stacks.
topSignals.text: Direct newsroom checks today confirm no new post: Elcogen's latest remains the Sept 21 Metrosert testing-cooperation announcement (24 days old); Topsoe's most recent SOFC/SOEC-specific item remains the Aug 27 H1 2026 results (49 days old). No new product, capacity, or partnership announcement from either in the 24-48h window. Elcogen News | Topsoe News

topSignals.title: Chaozhou Three-Circle (CCTC) gets its first-ever dedicated search in this monitor's benchmark rotation — and returns a blank.
topSignals.text: Today's six-company rotation (CCTC, Doosan Fuel Cell, Watt Fuel Cell, OxEon Energy, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol) found no new datapoint for any of the six; CCTC specifically has no public English- or Chinese-language SOFC/SOEC company news at all in the search results — only generic market-research-report listings and a Wikipedia profile. This remains an open coverage gap for INOCEL's benchmark tracking of this Chinese stack maker.

topSignals.title: New regulatory detail on Germany's data-center grid-fee economics: CMS Hamburg's Oct 1, 2026 "Re-Connect" update spells out the AgNes capacity-price reform and a 2031 phase-out of the "Bandlast" flat-load grid-fee privilege.
topSignals.text: Not previously logged at this level of detail. The Bundesnetzagentur's AgNes process would replace today's capacity-based grid price with a capacity price (loads >100,000 kWh) plus a two-part energy price, while the Bandlast privilege that many data centers rely on continues only for existing customers through end-2031, with no replacement yet decided (deferred to a 2027 follow-up). This is a grid-cost-escalation signal relevant to INOCEL's on-site-generation value proposition — see LCOE section. CMS Law

items.text: Elcogen (priority stack):* No new company news. Direct fetch of elcogen.com/category/news confirms the Sept 21, 2026 Metrosert cooperation announcement remains the latest post (24 days old; prior posts Sept 15 Shanghai HyEnergy and Aug 31 China Southern Power Grid MoU, both already on file). No capacity, efficiency, or partnership announcement found.

Topsoe (priority stack):* No new company news. topsoe.com/news still shows only the H1 2026 half-year results and the Uniper e-methanol FEED contract as the two most recent items (no dates shown on the page itself, consistent with the archive's standing record of Aug 27 and July items respectively). No new SOEC/SOFC test result, factory milestone, or partnership identified.

Rotating benchmark-company dedicated searches (this cycle, round 2: Chaozhou Three-Circle/CCTC, Doosan Fuel Cell, Watt Fuel Cell, OxEon Energy, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol), 7-day lookback, run as two combined sweeps plus individual follow-up:

Chaozhou Three-Circle (CCTC): First dedicated search for this company in the monitor. No company-specific SOFC/SOEC news located in English or Chinese; results were limited to generic global SOFC market-research-report listings (GII, SciEngine) that mention CCTC only as a named industry participant, plus its Wikipedia profile. No efficiency, capacity, or partnership data available — flagged as a standing data gap, to be re-tried in future rotations.

Doosan Fuel Cell: No new item. The $78M/≈£60M Reverion SOFC-stack supply contract (resurfaced via evertiq.com) is the already-logged Sept 18 deal; an enkiai.com "high-stakes SOFC pivot" explainer and a Q2 2026 earnings recap are commentary, not new disclosure.
Watt Fuel Cell: No new item; most recent substantive news (equity financing, first WATT HOME residential installation) remains from July 2026, outside this week's window.
OxEon Energy: No new item identified.
Kawasaki Heavy Industries: No SOFC-specific news found; results were generic corporate/stock coverage.
Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol: No new 2026-dated item; results were legacy technical publications, institute pages, and an older Korean-shipbuilding/Fraunhofer MoU unrelated to this window.

Other key players (Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin):* No new stack/cell-technology-specific announcements beyond items already logged (financial/market items for Bloom, FCEL and Ceres covered below). Sunfire's SOEC test facility at BASF Schwarzheide remains the most recent genuinely new stack-adjacent item on file, unchanged. A Hannover Messe 2026 recap of SolydEra's PMX platform (h2-international.com) resurfaced today but repeats previously logged technical details (G8X stack scaled to 10 kW, 60% electrical/84% total efficiency, DynElectro's 23,000h test) with no new figures. Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera and Aisin: no 2026-dated SOFC-specific news found; search results were 2025-vintage SEO-aggregator "strategy" pieces, consistent with the pattern flagged in prior entries.

New (see Top Signal #3):* CMS Hamburg's Oct 1, 2026 update on German data-center grid/power regulation. Beyond the AgNes/Bandlast detail above, it confirms: the TSOs' "Reifegradverfahren" grid-connection allocation process (first-ready-first-served, replacing first-come-first-served) has been in effect since April 1, 2026, with results expected end-November and litigation anticipated; the draft Netzpaket (§§17a-17e EnWG-RegE) would give this a statutory basis and add flexible-connection-agreement and capacity-reservation rules, targeted for year-end enactment; a draft EnEfG amendment would raise the renewables-coverage requirement for data centers from 50% to 100% but delay it to January 1, 2030; an EU draft delegated regulation plans a data-center sustainability label from August 2027 (adoption uncertain). CMS Law
